# Branch `os-windows`: Windows Laptop Guide

For any AI working on this branch (Claude Code on the Linux machine, GitHub Copilot on the Windows laptop).
It says what the branch is for, which machine you are on and what that allows, how to take new changes on the
laptop, and what has been done so far and why. The how-to for running the app on Windows is `.os_windows.md`;
the rules the code follows to stay cross platform are in `spec/services/ui/README.md` ("Platforms").

## What this branch is for

Make delulu-smash work on the user's **work Windows laptop**, without breaking it on Omarchy (Arch Linux),
where it is built. `main` stays the Linux line until the Windows work is done; then `os-windows` is merged
into `main` (no pull request).

The work is done on two machines that play different roles:

| | Linux machine (Omarchy) | Work Windows laptop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI | Claude Code | GitHub Copilot only: no Claude Code, no API keys, no Pydantic AI Gateway |
| Git | commits and **pushes** to `os-windows` | **pulls only**: commits locally, never pushes |
| Role | where changes are designed and written | where they are run and checked on real Windows |
| Edits made here | reach the laptop on its next pull | **stay on the laptop**: they never come back |

## First: which machine are you on?

Don't ask the user; run one command at the start of a session:

| Command | Output | You are on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uname -s` | `Linux` | the Linux machine |
| `uname -s` | `MINGW64_NT-...` or `MSYS_NT-...` (Git Bash) | Windows |
| `uname -s` | "not recognized" (PowerShell, cmd) | Windows |

- On Windows, assume the **work laptop** (pull only), unless the user says it is the Omarchy Windows VM
  (`.os_windows.md`, "In the Omarchy Windows VM"), which is a test box on the Linux machine.
- Say in a line which machine you found, the first time it matters in a session.

## Constraints of the work laptop

Each one is a reason behind something on this branch. Don't "fix" what they explain.

- **Pull only.** Never run `git push`, and don't suggest it. Local commits are fine and expected.
- **GitHub Copilot is the only AI.** No Claude Code, no model API keys, no Gateway key. So:
  - the app must start and be useful with no keys ("The app works without the AI" in the spec);
  - an AI feature there can only go through the Copilot seat: see `experimental/copilot_agent/` below;
  - Claude Code's own files (`CLAUDE.md` imports, `.claude/`, hooks, skills) do nothing there. Copilot is
    pointed here by `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- **No Git LFS.** The laptop can't fetch LFS files, so the parquet tables and fonts are plain git files on
  this branch. Don't re-add LFS tracking.
- **It is a managed work machine.** No admin rights are assumed; a policy may refuse things (eg the Task
  Scheduler task, which is why `ds ui install` falls back to a Startup shortcut). When something is
  refused, report what Windows said; don't work around the policy.
- **Windows itself**: no Unix-only modules, UTF-8 by name, no fixed `/usr/...` paths. The rules and the
  known gaps are in the spec's "Platforms" section.
- **Omarchy things don't exist there**: `.os/`, `os sync`, Hyprland, systemd. The laptop never edits `.os/**`.

A constraint found on the laptop that isn't listed: tell the user, so it is added here from the Linux machine.

## On the laptop: taking new changes

Commit local edits first, then pull with a rebase, so the laptop's own commits sit on top of what came in:

```bash
git add <files> && git commit -m "local: <what and why>"   # pull refuses to overwrite uncommitted edits
git pull --rebase
git log --stat ORIG_HEAD..HEAD        # exactly what arrived since the last pull, with each commit's why
uv sync                                # when uv.lock or a pyproject.toml arrived
```

Then read the arrived commits' messages (see "Commit messages" below): each says what was asked, why, and
what to do on the laptop after pulling.

### When the rebase stops on a conflict

**Mind the names**: during `git pull --rebase`, Git's "ours" / `HEAD` side is the **pulled** version, and
"theirs" is the **laptop's** commit being replayed. That is the reverse of a merge, so don't go by those
words: use "pulled" and "laptop's" as below.

| File or area | Resolve by |
| --- | --- |
| `uv.lock` | take the pulled one (`git checkout --ours uv.lock`), then `uv lock` |
| "What was really run on Windows" table in `.os_windows.md` | keep both sides' rows |
| `.os/**`, `.agents/**`, `.github/**`, `CLAUDE.md`, `spec/**` | pulled wins; the laptop doesn't edit these |
| `pkgs/**`, `services/**`, `tests/**`, `experimental/**` | pulled wins, then re-apply the laptop's edit on top only if it is still needed |
| the pulled commit already contains the laptop's fix | drop the laptop's commit: `git rebase --skip` |
| anything under `local/` | never conflicts (git-ignored): the place for laptop-only files |

After fixing a file: `git add <file>`, then `git rebase --continue`. To give up and go back to before the
pull: `git rebase --abort`.

- **Why pulled wins**: the laptop's commits never leave it, so the pulled version is the one both machines
  share. A laptop edit kept against it has to be re-applied on every later pull.
- **Before re-applying a laptop edit, read why the pulled change was made** (its commit message). If the two
  disagree in intent, not only in lines, stop and ask the user.
- **Keep the laptop's edits few and small.** A fix that belongs in the code for everyone (a bug, a missing
  Windows case): make it locally to keep going, and tell the user exactly what was changed and why, so it is
  redone on the Linux machine. Once it arrives by pull, the local commit is dropped as in the table.
- **Laptop-only settings** (paths, tokens, switches) go in `local/` or environment variables, not in a
  tracked file.

## Commit messages on this branch carry the context

The laptop's AI has no access to the sessions in which the changes were made, so the commit message is the
only context it gets. On the Linux machine, every commit on `os-windows` has this body (a line or two each):

```
ui: Windows background service + icon (Ctrl+Alt+J)

Asked: run the app in the background on Windows with an icon and a hotkey, as on Omarchy.
Why: on the laptop the app is otherwise started by hand in a console that must stay open.
Decided: Task Scheduler per user (no admin), Startup folder as the fallback when a policy
  refuses the task; Ctrl+Alt+J because a Windows shortcut's hotkey can't use SUPER.
After pull (Windows): run `ds ui install` once.
```

- **Asked**: what the user asked for, close to their words. **Why**: the constraint or problem behind it.
- **Decided**: the choices made, and what was turned down when that isn't obvious.
- **After pull (Windows)**: what to run or check on the laptop, or "nothing".
- A change that alters a constraint or the merge table above also updates this file in the same commit.

### The Copilot trial (`experimental/copilot_agent/`)

**The question**: the laptop has no Claude Code and no API keys, only a work GitHub Copilot seat. Can that
seat run the repo's own AI agent (`ds.ai`, built on Pydantic AI)? If yes, the app's AI features could work
there after all.

**What was found on the Linux machine, with the user's personal Copilot seat (2026-11-19)**:

- Pydantic AI ships a `github-copilot` provider. The `gh` CLI's login token (`gh auth token`) was accepted.
- The `ds.ai` smash agent answered through Copilot with its tools working, on `claude-haiku-4.5`,
  `claude-sonnet-5.5` and `gpt-6-luna`.
- Copilot serves Claude and Gemini ids on chat completions and GPT ids only on its Responses endpoint, so
  the script picks the model class from Copilot's own model list. `gpt-6-luna` is the default, at the
  user's request.
- Each question costs Copilot premium requests (the smash agent makes about 3 per question).

**Not known yet, and the reason this is on the laptop**: whether the **work** seat allows it. An
organization can restrict the models and the clients a seat may use. To find out, on the laptop:

```bash
uv run experimental/copilot_agent/copilot_agent.py models                 # is the seat usable at all
uv run experimental/copilot_agent/copilot_agent.py ask "hi" --bare        # a plain model, no tools
uv run experimental/copilot_agent/copilot_agent.py ask "Little Mac jab 1 damage and startup?"
```

Report the exact output to the user, above all an HTTP 401 / 403 from `models` (it tells a wrong token type
from an organization's policy). If the policy refuses it, stop there: don't look for another way in.
